row.question:
Given the chest X-ray findings and the clinical history of the 25-year-old farmer from India, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? Consider the presence of a well-defined cavity in the left lower zone with collapsed membranes and multiple cavities in the right apex, along with fibrotic changes and tracheal traction. 

A. Tuberculous lung abscess with atelectasis
B. Fungal colonization of tuberculous cavities
C. Spontaneously ruptured pulmonary hydatid cyst with concomitant tuberculosis
D. Primary lung cancer with secondary infection
E. Pneumonia with lung necrosis
F. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with emphysematous changes

reference.correct_choice_text: Spontaneously ruptured pulmonary hydatid cyst with concomitant tuberculosis

historical_prediction.json.raw_response:
Answer: C. Spontaneously ruptured pulmonary hydatid cyst with concomitant tuberculosis  
Reason: The clinical context (25-year-old farmer from India) and imaging findings—well-defined cavity in left lower zone with collapsed membranes (suggestive of detached endocyst/hydatid membrane), multiple apical cavities with fibrosis and tracheal traction—are classic for ruptured pulmonary hydatid cyst (often presenting with “water-lily sign” or membrane collapse) coexisting with post-primary tuberculosis, which is highly endemic in India. The combination explains both the acute cavity with membranes and chronic fibrotic changes.

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When bilateral symmetric coarse nodular opacities improve dramatically after immunosuppression (e.g., steroids), and cavitary or fibrotic features are absent
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect for preservation of lung volumes and absence of traction bronchiectasis or reticulation on follow-up to distinguish acute hemorrhage resolution from chronic granulomatous/fibrotic disease regression
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Requires adequate inspiration and comparable projection; unreliable if follow-up is CT misinterpreted as CXR

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When mediastinal opacity obscures one heart border and tracheal deviation is present on PA CXR
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect which cardiac border is silhouetted (left border loss = left mediastinal pathology; right border loss = right-sided) and confirm tracheal deviation direction—deviation away from mass side—and compare costophrenic angle blunting severity per side.
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable if both borders obscured or in severe cardiomegaly; requires adequate inspiration and centering.
